metadata.title: Removing a Stubborn Brake Drum from a 1995 Chevy K-2500 8600 GVW Pick-up
metadata.description: Video showing how to remove a stubborn brake drum from a 1995 Chevy K-2500 with a modified Harbor Freight puller. CAUTION: I forgot to put a strap around the drum and axle to prevent the drum from flying off. Although I was standing back out of the way, having it fly off the way it did shook me up a bit. After removing the drums, I found that both wheel cylinders were leaking. This is a typical problem on high mileage GM products. Leaking wheel cylinders and/or axle seals will cause the drum brake system to grab and sometimes slide the wheels due to contamination of the brake linings. I modified/used this tool for this job after an exhaustive search for a drum puller. No one seems to make one big enough for these big drums found on the 8600 GVW trucks. Mine were stuck on the axles like they were welded. I will clean the axle flange of all rust and apply some anti-seize grease before installing the new drums. My truck uses the 13" X 2.5" brake shoes and very large heavy drums.

summary.brief: A man uses a modified hydraulic puller to free rust‑stuck rear brake drums from a 1995 Chevy K‑2500.
summary.detailed: The video begins with the narrator explaining that the rear brake drums on his 1995 Chevrolet K‑2500 have become fused to the axle after years of pounding, penetrating oil and heating. He shows a Harbor Freight 12‑ton hydraulic gear puller that he has altered by adding chains, a strap and a bit of duct‑tape to hold the puller’s jaws on the back side of a drum. After positioning the puller, he steps back and slowly activates the hydraulic mechanism; the drum snaps loose with a loud pop and flies off. He repeats the same set‑up on the opposite side, noting that the second drum is tougher but still comes free after the puller is engaged. Throughout he warns viewers to keep a safe distance and to use a safety strap because a detached drum can become a projectile. After both drums are removed he discovers leaking wheel cylinders, a common issue on high‑mileage GM trucks.

action.detailed: Attach the modified hydraulic puller around each drum, secure it with chains and duct‑tape, stand back, operate the puller to pull the drum off the axle, and repeat the process on the opposite side.
action.actor: The video’s narrator, a man wearing a blue shirt, denim shorts and glasses
